name: Primary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood
aliases: Pediatric and Adult Primary Interstitial Lung Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ATS/ERS Consensus Classification for Interstitial Lung Disease

criteria.description: Progressive dyspnea and nonproductive cough persisting for more than 3 months
High-resolution CT showing reticular opacities, ground-glass attenuation, or honeycombing consistent with interstitial lung disease
Lung biopsy demonstrating interstitial fibrosis, inflammation, or alveolar septal thickening consistent with ILD
Exclusion of known causes such as connective tissue disease, environmental exposures, or drug-induced lung disease
Restrictive ventilatory defect with reduced diffusion capacity on pulmonary function testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation and characteristic radiologic pattern with exclusion of secondary causes; histopathology and pulmonary function tests supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pulmonology, radiology, and pathology.

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity
weakness related to low blood oxygen

common.symptomName: Dry mouth or ocular dryness (secondary Sjögren’s features)

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension symptoms (e.g., syncope, chest pain)
searchTerms: symptoms of high lung blood pressure
fainting and chest pain from lung hypertension
shortness of breath with chest discomfort

rare.symptomName: Weight loss due to chronic illness

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
Autoantibodies negative or low titer (to exclude connective tissue disease)
imaging: High-resolution CT demonstrating reticular opacities, ground-glass opacities, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis
Chest X-ray showing bilateral interstitial infiltrates
genetic: Rare familial cases with mutations in surfactant protein genes (e.g., SFTPC, SFTPA2) especially in childhood-onset
Telomerase complex gene mutations (TERT, TERC) in some adult cases
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity (DLCO)
Lung biopsy histology consistent with usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) or nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Extrapulmonary manifestations such as arthritis or rash

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
references: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002
Orphanet Report Series: Primary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood, Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 2023
Genetic and Clinical Features of Interstitial Lung Disease in Children and Adults, Chest, 2021
